## Does Park Designation Drive Crowd Size?

Every point in the scatterplot below represents one National Park Service unit in a single year between 1979 and 2025 (**16,095 park-year observations** in total). Grouping these observations by **Park Unit Type** reveals a surprising pattern: while flagship National Parks draw huge headlines, **Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways** actually hold the highest median attendance (~1.16 million visits per year), whereas **Historic Sites** and **National Monuments** make up the vast majority of locations with smaller, steadier crowds (~110,000 visits per year).

```{r}
#| label: fig-park-visitation-by-type
#| fig-cap: "Annual recreation visits across 16,095 park-year observations (1979–2025), colored by NPS unit category. Solid lines track the median attendance for each category each year."
#| column: body-outset
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-dpi: 300

library(tidyverse)

annual_visits <- read_csv(
  "nps_annual_visits_1979_2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    suffix = word(park, -1),
    park_type = case_when(
      suffix %in% c("NP", "NPRES", "PRES") ~ "National Parks & Preserves",
      suffix %in% c("NRA", "NS", "NL", "PKWY", "NR", "NSR", "W&SR", "NRRA") ~ "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways",
      suffix %in% c("NM", "Monument") ~ "National Monuments",
      TRUE ~ "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials"
    ),
    park_type = factor(
      park_type,
      levels = c(
        "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways",
        "National Parks & Preserves",
        "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials",
        "National Monuments"
      )
    )
  )

type_medians <- annual_visits |>
  group_by(year, park_type) |>
  summarize(
    median_visits = median(recreation_visits, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

top_2025 <- annual_visits |>
  filter(year == max(year)) |>
  slice_max(recreation_visits, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

palette_cols <- c(
  "Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways" = "#1D6996",
  "National Parks & Preserves" = "#2E6F40",
  "Historic Sites, Battlefields & Memorials" = "#CC792B",
  "National Monuments" = "#944654"
)

ggplot(annual_visits, aes(x = year, y = recreation_visits, color = park_type)) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.22, height = 0, seed = 2026),
    alpha = 0.18,
    size = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = type_medians,
    aes(y = median_visits, group = park_type),
    linewidth = 1.15
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = top_2025,
    color = "#1F3B2C",
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 2025,
    y = top_2025$recreation_visits,
    label = paste0("2025 Leader:\n", top_2025$park),
    hjust = 1,
    vjust = 1.25,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1F3B2C",
    fill = "#FFFDF9",
    label.size = 0.2
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 2020,
    y = 22000,
    label = "2020 COVID-19 dip",
    color = "#3A4A40",
    fontface = "italic",
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1980, 2025, by = 5),
    limits = c(1979, 2026)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = scales::transform_pseudo_log(sigma = 1),
    breaks = c(0, 10000, 100000, 1000000, 5000000, 10000000, 20000000),
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Every Park, Every Year: Visitation by NPS Unit Type (1979–2025)",
    subtitle = "16,095 park-year observations (dots) and annual category medians (solid lines)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Annual recreation visits (pseudo-log scale)",
    color = "Park Unit Category",
    caption = "Source: National Park Service Visitor Use Statistics (1979–2025)."
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      nrow = 2,
      byrow = TRUE,
      override.aes = list(alpha = 0.9, size = 2.5, linewidth = 1.3)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FCFBF7", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FCFBF7", color = NA),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1F3B2C", size = 16.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#4A6355"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#667085", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

## Key Takeaways from the Data

- **Recreation Areas, Seashores & Parkways lead in median crowd size:** With a median of **1.16 million annual visits**, scenic roadways, beaches, and urban recreation areas consistently draw larger typical crowds than remote parks.
- **National Parks & Preserves show steady multi-decade growth:** Across 3,394 park-year observations, flagship National Parks have grown to a median of over **537,000 annual visits**, with top units exceeding 10 million visitors.
- **Historic Sites & National Monuments form the backbone of the system:** Over two-thirds of all park-year observations (10,808 out of 16,095) belong to historical parks, battlefields, memorials, and monuments, which typically welcome around **105,000 to 123,000 visitors per year**.
